summary: A fourth bell rings beneath Faelspire. An impossible black fragment addresses the reader-character and forces a choice among P'taxx, Aard Templu Voreath, and a scarred stray who has heard the bell before.

active_frontiers.title: Make the Witness Work
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The protagonist committed to the seam: they turned their face to the opened seam, put the copy in the middle of the aim, and let the seam file the look-away under the copy's name. In doing so they paid the WANT in its exact currency — they became the subject of the reading they did not choose to be in. The lever is real, the copy works for the ledger, and the protagonist's record — the one that was never finished — is now being finished under their own name. The exit is still closed. The N1 reclassification beat (the witness → subject filing) is preserved. The next scene must address what it means to be the one the ledger is finishing, and whether a subject can still make a move the method does not expect.

active_frontiers.title: The Runner Corrects the Ledger
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: LEVER_REVERSED (pull leaf, extended). The protagonist's chosen act changed what the method works: they placed the sealed Mistral correction under the sheet's edge and pulled, and the method accepted the runner-supplied scroll as its new working target. The Mistral's record is corrected in the room — not filed, not re-closed — and the scroll is spent on the method's terms, not the palace's; the broken seal is a durable trace the palace will notice and will know which runner broke it. The method's aim at the protagonist remains revoked; the protagonist remains the working hand, paw on the lever, and the high door remains open while the hand works. The protagonist's own unfinished record is still open under the other paw — a respite, not a resolution; the method will turn back to it when it finishes the Mistral's sheet. P'taxx is still at the desk, still a subject; the want (get him out without surrendering the unfinished record) is unchanged, but the means have changed: the method now has a protagonist-chosen subject it can work. The next scene must address what the method does when it finishes the Mistral's record — whether the corrected name holds in the keeping, or whether the room re-closes it the way the palace closes things — and what the palace does when its seal comes back broken in a runner's satchel.

active_frontiers.title: The Correction Through the Door
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: LEVER_REVERSED (refuse leaf, extended). The protagonist's chosen act changed what the room keeps open: they passed through the narrowed door carrying the sealed Mistral correction, and the method — which outranks the keeping — took the runner-supplied scroll as the room's new open sheet. The Mistral's record is corrected in the room, not filed, not re-closed; the correction is the room's open sheet now. The keeping still holds the protagonist's own unfinished record open in the room — the protagonist has left it behind and is on the far side of a door that is the width of a shoulder and will not be wider again. The scroll is spent on the method's terms, not the palace's; the broken seal is a durable trace, and the palace, which signs its corrections out, will know which runner's paws were on it. P'taxx is still at the desk, still a subject; the want (get him out without surrendering the unfinished record) is unchanged, but the runner has left the record in the room and cannot carry it. The next scene must address what the room does with the corrected Mistral record — whether the corrected name holds in the keeping or the room re-closes it the way the palace closes things — and what the palace does when its seal comes back broken, and how the runner reaches P'taxx from the far side of a shoulder-width door that only opens inward.
